newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.03 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.03 pct to new record.

text.p: The market index at Istanbul's Stock Exchange closed at a new all-time high of 84,692.20 in highly selective activity on Monday, up 1.03 percent from Friday's previous record close of 83,828.67.
The IMKB-100 gained 863.53 points from Friday, but failed to pierce the critical 85,000 resistance, brokers said. It fell from an early noon high of 85,481 on profit-taking.
Trade volume was little changed at 21.52 trillion lira after Friday's 21.29 trillion.
"There was profit-taking because the index could not breach 85,000. Traders mostly switched shares," said Lokman Esref from Alan securities.
Some brokers said more fresh cash influx was needed to overcome the 85,000 barrier.

The index had drifted lower in a week-long limited pull back after testing 85,000 on October 31, following a 29.3 percent rally and ten record high closes in a strong medium-term uptrend from September 13 to October 23.
"The market may await tomorrow's Treasury auction to watch t-bill yields and then move accordingly," Esref said.
The Treasury will attempt to sell 182-day bills with Wednesday value on Tuesday.

T-bill and bond yields have been rising since last Tuesday's 273-day auction where demand fell sharply due to a 10 percent witholding tax imposed on interest income from government papers to be issued with 1997 maturity from November 1.

Top actives were utility Aktas Elektrik, up 6,000 lira at 103,000, largely state-owed petroleum refiner Tupras, down 750 lira at 22,000, utility Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,000 lira at 84,000 and T.Isbank's C series shares, up 1,000 lira at 14,750.
Together, the four made up 32 percent of the total volume.

Of the 226 shares traded, gainers outdid losers by 114 to 64 and 48 ended stable. The 85-share industrial index rose 1.05 percent to 89,245.76 and the 15-share financial index firmed 0.98 percent to 82,445.13.
